cases.exposure_context_quote: An 18-year-old woman presented to the emergency department 6 hours after ingesting approximately 5 mL of 24% PQ, taken with suicidal intent.
cases.agent: paraquat (24% solution, approximately 5 mL = 1.2 g; ~26 mg/kg)
cases.agent_quote: ingesting approximately 5 mL of 24% PQ, taken with suicidal intent

symptoms.finding: sore throat, epigastric pain, chest pain
symptoms.quote: On arrival at our center, she complained of sore throat, epigastric pain, and chest pain but denied difficulty breathing.

symptoms.finding: dysphagia and oral ulcers (tongue, lips, buccal mucosa) within 24 h
symptoms.quote: Within the first 24 hours, she developed dysphagia along with ulcers on her tongue, lips, and buccal mucosa.

symptoms.finding: severe high anion gap metabolic acidosis (day 3)
symptoms.quote: On day 3, arterial blood gasABG analysis revealed severe metabolic acidosis with a high anion gap.

symptoms.finding: early paraquat-induced pulmonary changes on chest X-ray (day 3)
symptoms.quote: A repeat chest X-ray performed on day 3 showed prominent bronchovascular markings in the right middle zone and slight heterogeneity in the bilateral lower zones

cases.time_to_care: 6 hours to our emergency department; taken to a nearby hospital 30 minutes after ingestion

labs.name: serum creatinine
labs.value: 1.0 mg/dL on admission rising to 7.3 mg/dL by day 6 (KDIGO stage 3 AKI)
labs.quote: serum creatinine rising from 1.0 mg/dL on the day of admission to 7.3 mg/dL by day 6 (eGFR declining from 83.7 mL/min/1.73m2 to 7.7 mL/min/1.73 m2)

labs.name: eGFR
labs.quote: serum creatinine rising from 1.0 mg/dL on the day of admission to 7.3 mg/dL by day 6 (eGFR declining from 83.7 mL/min/1.73m2 to 7.7 mL/min/1.73 m2)

labs.name: SGOT (AST)
labs.value: 16 U/L on presentation rising to 242 U/L on day 6
labs.quote: she had a significant rise in her transaminases (AST and ALT), which were 8 U/L and 16 U/L on the day of presentation, and they gradually increased to 242 U/L and 192 U/L on Day 6

labs.name: SGPT (ALT)
labs.value: 8 U/L on presentation rising to 192 U/L on day 6
labs.quote: she had a significant rise in her transaminases (AST and ALT), which were 8 U/L and 16 U/L on the day of presentation, and they gradually increased to 242 U/L and 192 U/L on Day 6

labs.name: leukocyte count
labs.value: 8680/µL baseline rising to peak 16,500/µL on day 5
labs.quote: The leukocyte count increased from a baseline of 8680/µL to a peak of 16 500/µL on day 5, showing a 90% increase above baseline

labs.name: urea
labs.value: 33 mg/dL day 1 rising to 289 mg/dL day 8 (Table 1)

treatment.name: gastric lavage and activated charcoal (at nearby hospital)
treatment.quote: Thirty minutes after ingestion, she was taken to a nearby hospital, where gastric lavage was performed and activated charcoal was administered.

treatment.name: ceftriaxone 1 g IV twice daily
treatment.quote: she was treated with antibiotics (ceftriaxone 1 g IV twice daily)

treatment.name: pantoprazole 40 mg IV twice daily
treatment.quote: a proton pump inhibitor (pantoprazole 40 mg IV twice daily)

treatment.name: dexamethasone 8 mg IV three times daily
treatment.quote: steroids (dexamethasone 8 mg IV three times daily)

treatment.name: N-acetylcysteine 1 g IV three times daily
treatment.quote: N-acetylcysteine 1 g IV three times daily, intravenous fluids, analgesics, and antiemetics

treatment.name: intravenous fluids, analgesics, antiemetics; NPO
treatment.quote: N-acetylcysteine 1 g IV three times daily, intravenous fluids, analgesics, and antiemetics. ... She was kept nil per oral NPO.

cases.outcome: survived; discharged day 7; no respiratory, gastrointestinal, or renal manifestations at 3-month follow-up
cases.outcome_quote: Three-month follow-up showed no respiratory, gastrointestinal, or renal manifestations.
cases.notes: Hemodialysis was indicated (severe high anion-gap metabolic acidosis) but not performed; family discharged her against medical advice on day 7 due to financial constraints. Follow-up was by video call only.
